content.title: The Morning Ledger — Front Page
content.teaser: Plain-spoken reporting for families, faith and the places we call home.

blocks.title: Parents Stand Up Against Federal Curriculum Mandates
blocks.summary: Lawmakers push back on federal overreach in school curriculum mandates, with parents from three counties rallying at the capitol.

blocks.title: The Family Is Still the Foundation of Our Towns
blocks.summary: Why the traditional family still anchors our communities, and what the latest census data really tells us.

blocks.title: Restored Letters Reveal Life on the Old Mill Road
blocks.summary: The county historical society unveils restored letters from the 1850s settlers who built the old mill road.

blocks.title: Thirty Years of Saturday Mornings at St. Anne's Pantry
blocks.summary: Church volunteers have stocked the food pantry every Saturday for thirty years. Meet the people behind the shelves.

blocks.title: Council Weighs Zoning Changes Residents Didn't Ask For
blocks.summary: Council weighs a new zoning plan that critics say will bring unwanted development to quiet neighborhoods.

blocks.title: Planting for Spring: An Autumn Gardening Guide
blocks.summary: As frost approaches, a master gardener walks through the bulbs, cover crops and root cellar tips worth doing this autumn.

blocks.title: Saving Seeds, Saving Traditions
blocks.summary: Heirloom tomato seeds, saved and shared, keep our family traditions growing year to year.

blocks.title: Faith, Family and Common Sense in Public Life
blocks.summary: Our columnist argues that faith and public life belong together, and that common sense should guide our schools.

blocks.title: Letters: Parents Know Best
blocks.summary: A reader letter defends the right of parents to choose what their children learn and when.

blocks.title: Ten Heritage Recipes From Our Readers' Kitchens
blocks.summary: Ten heritage recipes from the county cookbook, tested by our readers' grandmothers.

blocks.title: Your Holiday Calendar at a Glance
blocks.summary: What to know before the winter holidays: parish schedules, school closures and food drives.

links.description: Coverage of state and national policy and what it means for local families.
Reporting from our town halls, school boards and county offices.
Stories from congregations, church life and moral questions of the day.
Gardening, cooking and household traditions passed down through generations.
Archives, old photographs and the stories of the people who built this county.
Columns and letters from readers who believe in the family and the common good.
Get the weekly print edition delivered to your door each Thursday.
Church suppers, school events, library programs and town meetings.
